content.overview: Section 58 of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882 defines mortgage as the transfer of an interest in specific immovable property for the purpose of securing the payment of money advanced or to be advanced by way of loan, an existing or future debt, or the performance of an engagement which may give rise to a pecuniary liability. The transferor is the mortgagor; the transferee is the mortgagee. The section also defines the principal forms: simple mortgage, mortgage by conditional sale, usufructuary mortgage, English mortgage, mortgage by deposit of title deeds, and anomalous mortgage.
content.glance: Ask: (1) Transfer of interest in specific immovable property? (2) Purpose — secure debt or engagement? (3) Which form under s. 58? (4) Rights of redemption/sale as applicable?
content.study:
Mortgage is security, not an absolute transfer of ownership (contrast sale under s. 54). Identify the form — simple, conditional sale, usufructuary, English, deposit of title deeds, or anomalous — because rights and remedies differ.

No case holdings invented. Case-law verification remains a separate gate.

sections.heading: Definition
sections.body: Transfer of an interest in specific immovable property to secure a loan, debt, or engagement giving rise to pecuniary liability.

sections.heading: Forms
sections.body: Simple; by conditional sale; usufructuary; English; by deposit of title deeds; anomalous.

sections.heading: Security character
sections.body: Interest is transferred for security; equity of redemption remains with the mortgagor subject to the form.

sections.heading: Contrast with sale
sections.body: Sale transfers ownership for price; mortgage transfers a security interest.

provisions.title: Mortgage, mortgagor, mortgagee, mortgage-money and mortgage-deed defined

examples.title: Simple mortgage
examples.body: Owner transfers interest in land to secure a loan without delivering possession — simple mortgage under s. 58(b) framework.

hypotheticals.question: Does a mortgage transfer full ownership like a sale?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Mortgage transfers a security interest in specific immovable property; ownership remains with the mortgagor subject to the mortgage.

misconceptions.correction: s. 58 defines distinct forms; rights and remedies turn on the form used.

questionsAndAnswers.answer: Transfer of interest to secure debt; forms: simple, conditional sale, usufructuary, English, deposit of title deeds, anomalous.
